title: It’s a Small World --- Crossword on The Science of Networks
intro: This issue's crossword explores how the idea of networks appears in various domains such as brain wiring, food webs, epidemics, social connections, power grids, and the internet.
author: *Abhirup Mukherjee* [Department of Physics & Astronomy, Seoul National University]

CLUSTER: A group of nodes that are more densely connected to one another than to the rest of the network
EDGE: A connection between two points in a network graph
HUB: A highly connected point that can link distant parts of a network
INTERNET: The system formed by connected computers and networks around the world
NETWORK: A system of connected points through which information, energy, or influence can travel
PACKET: A small unit of data sent across a computer network
PATH: The route that connects two points in a network
ROUTER: A device that directs data between computer networks
WIFI: Wireless technology that connects devices to a local network

BIOME: A large ecological region characterized by its climate and typical communities of organisms
CASCADE: A chain reaction that spreads from one part of a system to another
CIRCUIT: A set of connected components through which electric current can flow
CONTAGION: The spread of an infectious disease through a population
FOODWEB: Map of who eats whom in an ecological community
GRAPH: A mathematical network made of points and the connections between them
NEURON: A nerve cell; one of the basic units in the brain’s communication network
NODE: A point in a network, such as a person in a social network
PATHWAY: A route through which a signal or process travels in a system
SYNAPSE: The junction where one neuron communicates with another
